learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to predict and analyze the flight dynamic behavior of a fixed-wing aircraft based on geometric properties, and to independently derive and interpret the relevant equations.
They can name the safety requirements of a passenger aircraft and independently derive the safety budgets for individual aircraft systems.
They are able to predict the failure probability of a system, as well as an aircraft crash or maintenance incident, based on the system architecture.
Furthermore, they are able to optimize the safety level of an aircraft system through technical measures.

syllabus_topics: Safety and real-time requirements for avionics systems
Basic structure and functional principles of avionics systems
Mathematical models for calculating the failure probability of individual aircraft systems
Analysis methods for evaluating the effects of system failure on the aircraft
Protection measures for avionics systems against environmental effects and random errors
Coordinate and reference systems of an aircraft
assessment_rules: The overall module grade for MABB640A is calculated with equal weighting from the grades of MABB611A and MABB612A. For each component (MABB611A and MABB612A), the assessment can be a graded written exam (60 min), a graded oral exam (20 min), or a graded presentation (20 min).
bibliography: Stephen Corda; Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
Bernard Etkin, Dynamics of Atmospheric Flight
